takeaways.label: Record standalone sales, profit hit by one-offs
takeaways.text: Standalone revenue reached an all-time high of ₹911 crores with all three segments growing double digits, while consolidated PAT dropped solely on ₹80.3 crores of exceptional items tied to AWUKO and Foskor exits.

takeaways.label: Ceramics is the star, guidance raised again
takeaways.text: Consolidated Ceramics growth guidance was revised up to 25–28% (from 23–25%), driven by Engineered Ceramics for Bloom Energy and Metallized Cylinders, with margin guidance also lifted.

takeaways.label: Abrasives margin compressed by input-cost spikes
takeaways.text: Standalone Abrasives margins fell to ~10% from a historical 15–16% as war-driven phenolic resin and oil-price increases could not be passed on quickly; management says margins have bottomed.

takeaways.label: Two troubled subsidiaries are being resolved now
takeaways.text: AWUKO entered asset-sale agreements and is proceeding to liquidation; Foskor Zirconia is expected to exit this quarter, removing a sustained drag on consolidated Electrominerals.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether standalone Abrasives margins begin their promised climb back toward 15%, the completion of the Foskor exit, and any initial revenue from the Hosur thin-wheel facility as customer qualifications progress.

points.label: Industrial Engineered Ceramics leading
points.text: The fastest-growing sub-segment is powered by two vectors: products for Bloom Energy (solid-oxide fuel cells) and Metallized Cylinders, both seeing strong demand pull.

points.label: All three geographies contributing
points.text: The U.S., Australia, and India subsidiaries are all performing well, driving the increase in consolidated-minus-standalone EBIT.

points.label: Refractories positioned in project-grade work
points.text: The business focuses on higher-temperature refractories tied to project orders rather than consumable refractories, and project-order momentum is strong.

points.label: Guidance raised twice in one year
points.text: From an initial 15–15.5%, consolidated Ceramics growth guidance was first revised to 23–25% and now to 25–28%; margin guidance was also lifted to 22.5–23.5% from 20.5–21%.

quotes.text: Rangarajan: "The trajectory of growth is projected based on the strong demand coming from these segments, and that is the logic of our projecting higher top-line growth as well as the margin expansion."

points.label: Broad-based volume growth
points.text: Precision, industrial, and retail segments all grew, aided by industrial activity, construction, infrastructure-led demand, new geographies, and new product introductions.

points.label: Precision side benefiting from CV cycle
points.text: The commercial-vehicle cycle is picking up, supporting good growth rates in the precision abrasives business.

points.label: Margins hit by sudden input-cost spikes
points.text: Standalone Abrasives margins dropped to ~10% from a historical 15–16% because war-driven price spikes in phenolic resins and oil-based inputs could not be passed on quickly, given limited stocking of these items.

points.label: Chinese import threat easing
points.text: The competitive pressure from Chinese abrasives is moderating as export-duty benefits were withdrawn and a strong dollar/weak rupee makes imports less attractive.

points.label: Margins have bottomed, recovery the focus
points.text: Management stated margins have bottomed out and the aim is to get back to the ~15% level, with work underway across multiple areas to address cost challenges.

quotes.text: Rangarajan: "the margins is bottomed out is my view... we would get back. But the trajectory we should aim to get to, a level of say, 15%, that is our normal trajectory that we should aim for."

points.label: AWUKO liquidation underway
points.text: In October 2026, AWUKO entered agreements to sell all property, plant, equipment, and inventory for ₹5.34 crores, reached a social plan with all employees under German labor law, and is now proceeding to final liquidation and de-registration.

points.label: AWUKO exceptional charge booked
points.text: A ₹18.3 crores exceptional item was recognized in Q2 FY27 for asset write-downs and restructuring costs; no further write-offs are expected, and operational losses were negligible this quarter.

points.label: Foskor Zirconia exit imminent
points.text: The exit is realistically expected to complete in the current quarter (before December); the business was determined commercially unviable due to sustained losses, rising input costs, and market pressures.

points.label: Foskor accounting conservative
points.text: The asset is already brought to realizable-basis reporting and fairly provided for; management expects no extraordinary challenge in concluding the exit.

points.label: Zirconia sourcing secure post-exit
points.text: CUMI's current zirconia facility is independent of the South Africa capability, with an established source and no disruption expected.

points.label: Domestic and export demand solid
points.text: Growth came from both Indian and international refractory and abrasive customers.

points.label: Consolidated sequential drop is Foskor-driven
points.text: The QoQ decline in consolidated Electrominerals revenue was predominantly due to lower sales at Foskor Zirconia, not the core business.

points.label: Standalone margin dip temporary
points.text: The QoQ margin decline was attributed to product mix and industry-served mix, described as not significant and expected to recover.

points.label: Imports becoming less competitive
points.text: A strong dollar/weak rupee is making imported electrominerals more expensive, which is expected to taper import volumes.

points.label: Value-add products offer pricing power
points.text: Treated and specialty electrominerals (heat-treated, chemically treated, coated) go to the same refractory and abrasive industries but are easier to pass costs through because of their value-add nature.

sections.title: New Growth Vectors: Semiconductor, Substrates, Armor

points.label: Semiconductor equipment components
points.text: Revenues are expected to start picking up from FY28, with peak potential of ₹300–350 crores around FY30–31, built in phases of expansion.

points.label: Electronic substrate program progressing
points.text: Technology support is secured from anchor customers, base-level works have been initiated, and the program will take at least a year before completion; CUMI is targeting value-added substrate, not mere substrate alone.

points.label: Armor line
points.text: A capex outlay of ~₹50 crores was mentioned.

points.label: New-area margins above baseline
points.text: In a stable state, PBIT margins for semiconductor, electronic substrates, and armor are expected to be higher than the baseline 20–21%.

points.label: Hosur thin-wheel facility
points.text: The new facility is established and working with 6–7 major international customers through the qualification process; the program is well on track.

quotes.text: Rangarajan: "We expect the top line from this segment could be somewhere in the range of about INR 300 crores to INR 350 crores."

points.label: YOY decline is a base-effect story
points.text: Q1 FY26 had a EUR 4–5 million shortfall from an operational transition that was picked up in Q2 FY26, creating an elevated base; sequential softness is regular seasonality.

points.label: Full-year outlook trimmed
points.text: Previously expected 5% growth with a small PAT loss; now expected to be flat on top line versus last year, with a loss lower than last year.

points.label: Turnaround program deployed
points.text: A large program is in place with a local team and management consultants to speed up the recovery; the path is break-even by Q1 of next year, then small profits building from there.

points.label: Prior warehouse disruption resolved
points.text: Losses are declining because the warehouse move that caused the top-line shortfall and higher costs is now behind the business, and margins are improving.

items.title: Group 2x growth target
items.text: Management's five-year strategy (May 2025) targets doubling revenue over five years with sustained profitability, anchored on scaling core businesses, new growth vectors and manufacturing excellence. Against FY26 revenue of ₹5,585 cr, that implies roughly ₹11,000 cr by FY30, with Aspiration 2030 programs reported on track as of Q2 FY27.

items.title: Semiconductor equipment ceramics
items.text: The Hosur facility's first module is commissioned (₹66 cr capex), global OEM anchor customers are qualified for serial supply, and management expects revenue to pick up from FY28, peaking at ₹300-350 cr over FY30-31 with total investment scaling 3-4x. That is roughly 5-6% of current group revenue at margins above the ceramics baseline of ~20-21%.

items.title: SOFC ceramics for data-centre demand
items.text: CUMI supplies a leading SOFC maker doubling capacity from 1 GW to 2 GW, with line of sight to ~2028 and the highest-ever order from these customers bagged in Q3 FY26; engineering ceramics grew 30% in FY26. Management sees SOFC potentially exceeding 10% of sales in about three years, driving the upgraded FY27 ceramics guidance.

items.title: Electrominerals exports and treated mix
items.text: Standalone exports doubled FY25→FY26 to over ₹300 cr (33% of sales vs 11%), helped by EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese grains, with a 40% export trajectory now targeted. Backing this, a white fused alumina furnace upgrade (₹53 cr capex, up to ₹95 cr revenue potential) and a treated grains facility (₹30 cr, up to ₹120 cr) start commercial production over FY27.

items.title: Thin Wheels Hosur plant
items.text: Commercial production started 16 March 2026 on DRONCO-acquired lines, doubling thin wheel capacity from 4.5 to over 9 crore wheels a year at ₹83 cr investment, with peak turnover guided at ₹160 cr. Qualification is underway with six to seven major international customers as of Q2 FY27.

items.title: Metallized cylinders expansion
items.text: CUMI is the world's number-two metallized cylinder producer, growing ~20% in the Nov 2025 quarter on the global shift from gas-insulated to vacuum-interrupter switchgear. A three-phase capacity expansion over 18-24 months, plus de-bottlenecking, is planned to substantially lift capacity by 2030.

items.title: AMB/DBC power-electronics substrates
items.text: CUMI is entering AMB and DBC substrates for power electronics, with an anchor-customer program underway: validation done, trials and first articles due in FY27, and a technology transfer agreement signed with capacity augmentation in FY27. The program needs about a year more to complete, adding a value-added product line on top of its number-two metallized cylinders position.

items.title: Defence armour ceramics
items.text: The ₹49 cr Hosur armour facility is commissioned with NIJ 3/4, BIS Threat Level 5/6 and STANAG 4 qualifications secured, and commercialisation progressing through anchor customers. Management expects the program to kick in from FY28 and scale up by 2030, pending SCOMET approval to expand exports.

items.title: Rhodius turnaround
items.text: Rhodius's FY27 loss narrowed to EUR 0.3 mn in Q2 from EUR 0.7 mn QoQ after the warehouse-transition sales loss is being recovered, with guidance of flat sales and a lower full-year loss. Management targets break-even by Q1 of next year, then small profits building up.

items.title: Loss-maker exits
items.text: Awuko's winding up is in final liquidation with property sale agreed and no further write-offs expected, and the Foskor Zirconia exit is expected to complete by December 2026. Together these address the over ₹100-120 cr of annual losses from loss-making subsidiaries, directly lifting group PAT from FY28.
